evals.prompt: I get 'Processing frame failed with code 15' running python3 scan.py on Ubuntu with the Scandit Linux SDK.
evals.expected_output: Status 15 = app ID mismatch; on Linux the app ID is the executable name = python3, not scan.py; key with the right or no executable name.

assertions.text: The answer says status 15 is an app ID / executable-name mismatch
The answer says the executable name for a Python script is python3, not scan.py
The answer suggests a key with the right executable name or without an executable name
The answer points only to public resources (Scandit docs, the dashboard, support@scandit.com)

evals.prompt: Linking fails on our Debian 10 box: undefined reference to `log@GLIBC_2.29' from libscanditsdk.so (SDK 8.6). dpkg installed the package without complaints.
evals.expected_output: The system glibc is too old; the SDK needs glibc 2.31 or newer since 7.0 (Ubuntu 20.04 / Debian 11), and the package can install but fail at link or load time; check ldd --version; upgrade the OS.

assertions.text: The answer says the glibc is too old for the SDK
The answer gives 2.31 or newer as the requirement (Ubuntu 20.04 / Debian 11 or newer)
The answer explains that a successful install does not mean the system meets the glibc requirement: the error appears at link or load time
The answer suggests ldd --version and an OS upgrade (e.g. Debian 11 / Ubuntu 20.04 or newer)

evals.prompt: Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3 with sc_camera: 'Could not request buffers: Cannot allocate memory'. I request the maximum resolution the camera reports.
evals.expected_output: The driver reports a stepwise range with an unrealistic maximum (e.g. 16376x16376); request a real sensor mode; check the return of sc_camera_request_resolution; query the mode with sc_camera_get_resolution_mode.

assertions.text: The answer explains the stepwise range with an unrealistic maximum (e.g. 16376×16376)
The answer says to request a real sensor mode (datasheet or v4l2-ctl --list-formats-ext)
The answer mentions checking the return value of sc_camera_request_resolution(
The answer mentions sc_camera_get_resolution_mode( with discrete vs stepwise (or v4l2-ctl --list-formats-ext) to see what the camera offers

evals.prompt: How do I enable inverted (light-on-dark) Data Matrix codes in Python?
evals.expected_output: settings.symbologies[sc.SYMBOLOGY_DATA_MATRIX].color_inverted_enabled = True in addition to enabling the symbology; only QR/MicroQR inverted by default.

assertions.text: settings.symbologies[sc.SYMBOLOGY_DATA_MATRIX].color_inverted_enabled = True is shown
The symbology itself is enabled too (enable_symbology or .enabled = True)
The answer says scanner.apply_settings(settings) is needed afterwards
No Python method or property is used that is not in the 8.6 bindings

evals.prompt: Is there some setting I can tweak to make the Linux SDK scan blurry codes better?
evals.expected_output: Only documented options; explain physical causes (focus, motion, exposure, PPM), documented options (HIGH_EFFORT etc.), and support contact.

assertions.text: Every setting the answer suggests is a documented API or JSON setting from the skill references (e.g. SC_PRESET_HIGH_EFFORT, code direction hint, search area)
The answer does not set settings by name strings other than documented JSON keys and symbology extensions
The answer explains blur causes (focus, motion, exposure) and pixels per module
The answer offers Scandit support (support@scandit.com) with original frames for hard cases

evals.prompt: After upgrading from 7.4 to 8.2 only one code per image is returned.
evals.expected_output: Multi-scan off by default; set_max_number_of_codes_per_frame removed in 8.0 → set_multi_scan_enabled + set_max_num_locations_to_process_per_frame; JSON key replaced; tracking feature.

assertions.text: The answer says multi-scan is off by default
sc_barcode_scanner_settings_set_multi_scan_enabled( and sc_barcode_scanner_settings_set_max_num_locations_to_process_per_frame( are named
The answer says set_max_number_of_codes_per_frame was removed in 8.0 (and JSON maxNumberOfCodesPerFrame is ignored)
The answer mentions the "tracking" license feature

evals.prompt: broken_descr.py processes my label but returns status 5 or finds nothing. The same image works with the C sample.
evals.expected_output: first_plane_row_bytes and memory_size are not properties of the 8.x ImageDescription; Python silently creates attributes; the stride is never set → use descr.set_plane_row_bytes(0, frame.strides[0]); contiguous buffer.

assertions.text: The answer says first_plane_row_bytes and memory_size are not properties of sc.ImageDescription in the 8.x bindings
The answer explains Python silently creates a plain attribute, so the stride is never set
The fix uses descr.set_plane_row_bytes(0, ...) with the array's stride (strides[0]) or 3 * width for a contiguous BGR frame
The fix keeps sc.IMAGE_LAYOUT_BGR_8U for the BGR frame (or converts to grey with GRAY_8U)
The answer suggests checking the apply_settings status (is_success()) as well

evals.prompt: sc_recognition_context_new returns a valid pointer, so my license key must be fine, right? But nothing ever scans.
evals.expected_output: A wrong key doesn't make context creation fail; the license status comes from sc_barcode_scanner_apply_settings / process_frame; print code and message.

assertions.text: The answer says context creation succeeds even with a wrong or missing key
The answer says the license status is reported by sc_barcode_scanner_apply_settings( and/or sc_recognition_context_process_frame(
The answer says to print the status code and the message (sc_byte_array_get_string(status.message))

evals.prompt: My settings JSON has "maxNumberOfCodesPerFrame": 5 but the Linux SDK 8.6 still returns one code per frame. No error is reported.
evals.expected_output: The key was removed in 8.0 and unknown keys are silently ignored; use multiScanEnabled + maxNumLocationsToProcessPerFrame; check as_json; tracking feature.

The replacement keys "multiScanEnabled" and "maxNumLocationsToProcessPerFrame" are given
The answer recommends checking sc_barcode_scanner_settings_as_json(
The answer mentions the "tracking" license feature
